name: SmartSearch

paper.title: SmartSearch: How Ranking Beats Structure for Conversational Memory Retrieval

retrieval.query: SpaCy NER/POS-weighted terms; entity discovery and PRF expansion
retrieval.candidates: exact substring grep; ColBERT dense fallback for ~1% of queries

use.context: ranked raw passages within budget (~3.1K tokens on LoCoMo)
use.reasoning: answer LLM call; answer prompt varies by protocol

stages.ingestion: Raw, unstructured conversation history is stored as passages with no LLM structuring at ingestion.
stages.retrieval: Query parsed with SpaCy into NER/POS-weighted terms (PROPN 3.0 > NOUN 2.0 > VERB 1.0, +1.0 for entities); exact substring matching (grep) for recall with rule-based entity discovery for multi-hop and pseudo-relevance feedback; ColBERT dense fallback (~1% of queries). Candidates reranked by mxbai-rerank-large-v1 CrossEncoder + ColBERT fused by weighted RRF (0.7/0.3), then truncated by fixed word budget or score-adaptive threshold (alpha * max CE score).
stages.answer: Top passages within the token budget are given to the answer LLM (gpt-4o-mini or gpt-4.1-mini depending on protocol).

summary: Fully deterministic retrieve-then-rank pipeline over raw conversation text (NER-weighted grep + CrossEncoder/ColBERT RRF + score-adaptive truncation), arguing ranking, not ingestion-time structure, is the bottleneck.
notes:
Authors: Derehag, Calva, Ghiurau (Midbrain). No code URL found in the paper text. Index-free variant drops ColBERT entirely and relies on grep + query expansion + single CrossEncoder. Paper explicitly warns LoCoMo numbers under the EverMemOS protocol and the MemOS protocol are not comparable (full-context swings 77.1 -> 91.2). AXES-CHECK: seed taxonomy row matches; note ColBERT is used as dense-retrieval fallback and as second ranker (indexed variant only).
DESIGN: Sec 3.1-3.6, 4.4, Fig. 1. trigger null: paper does not describe when history is appended.
